source: EARS (Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax), Mavin et al., plus this project's dataset convention
note: Small enough to include in full in every LLM prompt.

patterns.name: Ubiquitous
patterns.example: The flight control computer shall compute attitude at 50 Hz.

patterns.name: Event-driven
patterns.example: When an overheat condition is detected, the FCC shall shut down the affected channel.

patterns.name: State-driven
patterns.example: While on battery power, the system shall enter low power mode.

patterns.name: Unwanted Behavior
patterns.syntax_template: If <trigger/condition>, then the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.example: If the primary sensor fails, then the software shall switch to the backup sensor.

patterns.name: Optional Feature
patterns.syntax_template: Where <feature is included>, the <system name> shall <system response>.
patterns.example: Where automatic braking is selected, the autobrake controller shall modulate brake pressure based on wheel slip ratios.

patterns.name: Complex
patterns.syntax_template: While <state>, when <trigger>, the <system name> shall <system response>. (any combination of the state-driven/event-driven/unwanted-behavior/optional-feature clauses, in that clause order, ahead of a single 'shall' response)
patterns.example: While in autonomous approach mode, if the primary altimeter fails, the flight control computer shall transition to the backup altimeter within 200 milliseconds.
